data.narrative:
ARC Clean Technology, founded by Don Wolf, is a Series G nuclear energy company that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 8 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private peers (Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy)—operating in the nuclear energy sector.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the company's $14M total-raised proxy as a base and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement. This method yields an implied valuation of $18M. Peer-median triangulation cannot be reliably applied; while 5 same-sector private comparables exist, none satisfy narrow peer filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) with sufficient datapoint density (minimum 3 required). Broadening to all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given the sector-specific capital intensity of nuclear technologies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M (low) to $21M (high), with a median point of $18M. This single-method conclusion carries meaningful uncertainty. The constrained peer set reflects both the nascent stage of frontier nuclear and the difficulty sourcing directly comparable companies at Series G maturity. Additional clarity on ARC's capital efficiency, project advancement milestones, and regulatory pathway would refine this range materially.
